summary: Koichi Shinohara works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He served as Professor at McMaster University (~1972–2004), coordinator of the Numata Program at the University of Toronto Mississauga, and Senior Lecturer in Religious Studies at Yale University (~2004–2020).

Koichi Takahashi specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Tokyo (~1996–2004) under supervisors Yasunori Ejima and Akira Saito, and held a post as an assistant (助手) there (~2004–2005).

Koichi Yokoyama studied Buddhist studies and philosophy, earning an MA at the University of Tokyo (~1968–1973) under Akira Hirakawa, and studied under Gyoin Hashimoto in 1970. He served as assistant professor (助教授) at Rikkyo University (~1976–2006).

Koji Kamioka specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at Kyoto University (~1961–1969) under Yutaka Ochihara, held a post at Kyoto Sangyo University (~1969–1975), and served as assistant professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1975–2001).
Specializing in Buddhist studies, Koji Takahashi studied at Bukkyo University (~1953–1962). He later served on the faculty there as an assistant professor (助教授) from approximately 1968 to 2005.

Kojun Bessho is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He has held positions as a full-time researcher (常勤研究員) at Chisan Denpoin and as a researcher (研究員) at the Kawasaki Daishi Institute of Buddhist Studies.

Kojun Fukui worked in Buddhist studies and Sinology. After studying at Waseda University (~1920–1926), he held a post there (~1935–1969) and later served as president (学長) of Taisho University (~1974–1978).
Kojun Saito specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Seiren Matsunami and served as a Lecturer at Taisho University from approximately 1962 to 1965.
Kokan Fujita is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Yujun Endo. He has held a post as professor (教授) at Koyasan University.
Koken Sasaki specialized in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Rissho University (~1950–1960) and later served there as Director and Professor (~1968–2002).

Koken Unno earned a doctoral degree from Nagoya University by 2000, studying under Yoshifumi Ueda, Hakuju Ui, and others. His career in Buddhist studies and Indology includes posts at Nagoya University, Aichi Prefectural University of Fine Arts and Music, and Meijo University.
Koki Kawagishi is a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies. He has served as a professor (教授) at both Eizan Gakuin and Shitennoji University.
Konrad Klaus specializes in Indology and Tibetology. He studied under Michael Hahn (~1980–1986) and became a Professor at the University of Bonn around 2001.

Kosei Ishii studied at Waseda University (~1969–1974), serving there as assistant in 1986. His career in Buddhist studies and philosophy includes posts at Komazawa Junior College (~1986–1995), Nagoya University as professor, and Komazawa University as professor (~1995–2021).

Kosei Mizutani worked in Buddhist studies, completing his education at Bukkyo University (~1945–1949) and Ryukoku University (~1949–1953). He later held a post as assistant professor (助教授) at Bukkyo University (~1957–1999).

Kosei Tada was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1963–1968). He held a post at Taisho University (~1974–2009) and served as board chairman (理事長) of the Society for Buddhist Cultural Studies.
Koshin Suzuki works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University by ~1993 and held an appointment there as a researcher (研究員).

Koshiro Tamaki studied at the University of Tokyo (~1937–1940). Working in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, he held posts at Toyo University (~1957–1965), University of Tokyo (~1965–1976), Tohoku University (~1972–1976), and Nihon University (~1976–1985).

Kosho Kawamura studied at Toyo University (~1948–1952) under mentors including Giyu Nishi and Koshiro Tamaki. His career in Buddhist studies and Indology included posts at Toyo University (~1955–1994), Minobusan University, Hamamatsu University, and Nava Nalanda Mahavihara.
Kosho Uchiyama was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Waseda University (~1934–1937). He studied under Kodo Sawaki (~1940–1965) and later succeeded him.
